report:
Reviewed the full owned_products claim and all three ordinary implementation entries after adding missing associations for body finalization and rooted storage. Requirements are: immutable CST/source input, a fresh output stash per signature/body, a self-contained Stashed result, and content-based deterministic comparison for backdating independent of arena address/source-tree lifetime. Check stores source_stash as a shared reference, constructs target_stash with Stash::new, allocates completed predicate lists there, and finish moves that stash into Stashed. finalize_typed_body likewise accepts shared source storage, constructs a fresh target, recursively copies expression, type, pattern, statement, call-target, and slice edges, and moves the completed root and target into Stashed. LocalVar contains only name and relative span, so allocating its slice does not preserve source-stash handles. The result type owns its stash rather than borrowing the source. FingerprintHasher recursively hashes pointed-to content and slice length/elements; entry indices are cache keys, not the fingerprint payload. Stashed::new computes the root fingerprint, PartialEq compares fingerprints, and its Salsa Update returns unchanged for equal fingerprints. These provide the content comparison boundary; database identities may remain database-scoped and this claim does not require fingerprints to persist across independently constructed databases.

The complete associated test set contains one ordinary test and one explicit TODO. body_finalization_resolves_types_into_a_fresh_stash constructs a tuple with an inferred element, finalizes it, asserts the source inference entry remains unchanged, and navigates the completed stash to assert the tuple element is i32. Thus assertions exercise source preservation and target ownership/resolution for this nested case; they would detect retained unresolved source type data. It is a focused unit test, not exhaustive source-driven signature/body or incremental verification. The TODO checking_owned_products explicitly defers structural checks for source-stash/tree-sitter references, equal-recomputation fingerprints, and persistent-edit downstream reexecution suppression. This is an accepted visible test deferral, not passing functional evidence: prerequisites are a structural output traversal with distinct source/output ownership fixtures, independent equal-product recomputation fixtures, and a persistent database/edit/query-trace scenario demonstrating downstream suppression. These scenarios include signature coverage, source lifetime independence, allocation-layout variation, and backdating integration that the single ordinary test cannot establish. There are no N/A entries or deferred implementation entries. The architectural-foundations rationale captured in this review agrees with fresh owned storage and structural copying.

Executed cargo test -p sage-ir body_finalization_resolves_types_into_a_fresh_stash --lib: 1 passed, 0 failed. Executed cargo fmt and cargo build successfully after comment-only implementation-association additions. Source inspection and the focused test support the implemented boundary; comprehensive verification remains explicitly TODO. No behavioral change or regression was introduced, and no further edits are requested.
